key_insight: PFM and related nanoscale measurements indicate that methylammonium lead iodide perovskite thin films contain ~90 nm ferroelectric domains with alternating polarization.
engineering_relevance: These ferroelectric/piezoelectric domain structures may influence local charge separation and extraction in perovskite solar cells, affecting device performance and variability.
method: Vertical and horizontal piezoresponse force microscopy to map polarization domains
High-resolution photo-conductive AFM under illumination to probe charge carrier extraction patterns
AFM and Kelvin probe force microscopy to correlate topography, surface potential, and ferroic behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent alternating domain patterns across PFM, illuminated photoconductive AFM, AFM, and KPFM, supporting the interpretation of polarized ferroelectric and piezoelectric domains.
watch_item: The findings are based on nanoscale microscopy correlations, so translating domain behavior into stable device-level benefits or controls requires further validation under operating conditions.
paper_title: Ferroelectric domains in methylammonium lead iodide perovskite thin-films
